The following is one possible way to set up a website from start to finish, which will allow you to build websites from start to finish. If you want to use a content management system (CMS) like Wordpress, then you will need to look up a separate tutorial for that. It assumes that you already at have at the bare minimum a computer or server to use as a webserver.

Step 1, selecting the operating system (OS) for your webserver. In general, you will want to use some form of Linux, but Windows and MacOS can also be used for webhosting as well. For the sake of this tutorial, use Ubuntu. Ubuntu is one of the major distributions of Linux, and is free. The download link to the latest, stable, long-term support version is here: http://www.ubuntu.com/download/server. Download that, put it on a bootable USB drive or DVD, and put it onto your webserver.

Step 2, setting up your webserver. Visit the following link to learn how to set up a basic webserver: https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/how-to-install-linux-apache-mysql-php-lamp-stack-on-ubuntu. The Linux OS is to run the rest of the basic software. Apache is used to listen to incoming requests for pages and make sense of it. With these two, you will be able to make basic HTML page websites. The addition of PHP allows you to easily handle server-side scripting. The addition of MySQL further allows you to save data that persists throughout and beyond individual user sessions in your website. There are better replacements for MySQL now (e.g. MariaDB, PostgreSQL), but for the sake of following the online tutorial, just use MySQL.

Step 3, reserve a domain name. You will need to reserve a domain name from a domain name registrar, and have it point to your webserver's IP address. This will likely require an annual or bi-annual fee. You can do an online search for domain registrars and pick one you like.

Step 4, configuring your webserver. In the most basic case, your server will only be using a single IP address. If you want to allow it to handle incoming requests from other IP addresses, then Apache will need to be configured. You will also definately need to set up a virtual host pointing to a web root folder. Instructions for that can be found at https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/how-to-set-up-apache-virtual-hosts-on-ubuntu-16-04.

Step 5, website stuff. At this point, you should have a domain name that points to an empty folder. Now, you need to decide what kind of website you want, and what you will need to learn in order to create it. A basic website will at the very least require knowledge of HTML. If you want to change the way that things look, you will need to learn about CSS. If you want to do any kind of client-side scripting, you will need to learn Javascript. If you want to do any kind of server-side scripting, you will need to learn PHP. If you want to save any data permanently, you will need to learn how to use MySQL. You can do an online search for tutorials on each of these. If you don't feel like doing that, here's the first result: http://www.yourwebskills.com.
